correctness.rationale: The published Apéry Lucas congruence and exact initial values \(1,5,73,1445,33001\) show the allowed base-five digits are exactly \(0,2,4\). Adding a fixed base-five shift has a single forced carry branch at each digit, with explicit weight vectors \((3,1),(1,2),(2,2),(2,1),(1,3)\). The terminal carry equals h mod 2, yielding \(Q_r(h)=3^{r-L}\) times the product for even h and zero for odd h at every \(r\ge L\). Only neutral factors (carry,digit)=\((0,0),(1,4)\) can equal one; classifying paths with one or two factors \(2/3\) gives the exact sharp maxima and their equality families. The proof is all-depth; the checker verifies its finite test ranges independently.

value.rationale: The Apéry five-nondivisible indices have zero natural density, making the ordinary two-point density identically zero and uninformative. Their natural sparse-scale normalized additive self-intersection \(Q_r(h)/3^r\) is a motivated new invariant. The theorem evaluates it for every shift and identifies exact first and second global overlap levels with complete extremizer families. This supplies structural information about pairwise divisibility dependence in a classical arithmetic sequence, not just a re-labelled digit set or a one-point congruence.
